subject: Redwood vs CloudScale latency/throughput lab — scope & next decisions
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Beth White <beth.white@acme.ai>, Tom Rhee <tom.rhee@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: proposed latency/throughput lab & decision map

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on what matters for Acme's inference workload. Quick recap + concrete proposal so we can lock the lab schedule and success criteria.

Summary of priorities from the call:
- Primary metric: p99 token latency for 1k token sequences under baseline concurrency patterns (spiky bursts and steady 50 RPS).
- Secondary metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec (tokens processed per GPU-second), and cost per 1M tokens at steady state.
- Workloads: mix of short (64 tokens), medium (256 tokens), and long (1024 tokens) sequences; sample prompt set provided by Acme.

Proposed A/B lab (high level):
1) A: CloudScale managed endpoint (their latest gen-large) — run under the same request pattern Acme shared.
2) B: Redwood hosted inference using our optimized runtime (quantized FP16 path + KV-prefix cache).
3) Same synthetic/conversation workload, identical concurrency profile, identical prompt set and RNG seeds where applicable.

Success criteria / acceptance signals (suggested):
- Redwood p99 <= CloudScale p99 - 15ms for medium/long sequences OR comparable p99 with >=20% lower tokens/sec cost.
- Tokens/sec improvement (throughput) measured at 95% utilization targets.
- No correctness regressions on Acme’s prompt set (use their 50 critical prompts checked for semantic parity).

Next steps I propose:
- Acme to share the canonical prompt set + representative concurrency profile (we already have a partial set, request the full 50).
- Redwood to deliver a lab plan (test matrix, timings, required access) by EOD tomorrow — attached is the draft plan.
- Schedule a mid-lab sync and a final readout (45 min).

Attachments: redwood-proposed-lab-plan.xlsx (draft test matrix and infra checklist); redwood-vs-cloudscale-metrics-spec.md (metrics collection/definitions).

Questions for you both:
- Any constraints on IP or data we should account for in the lab environment? (e.g., samples that cannot leave Acme infra)
- Is CloudScale running behind a VPC connector we need to peer for direct comparisons, or will you run their managed endpoint with us driving requests?

If everyone is good with the plan I’ll ask Grace and Dev to finalize the runbook and test scripts. Want to start runs no later than next Tuesday (21 Sep) to keep things moving for Q4 planning.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — this lines up with what we need. A couple quick clarifications before you finalize the runbook: 

1) Priority metric: please prioritize p99 for 1024-token sequences — that’s the worst-case that impacts our user SLAs.
2) Cost metric: include an explicit "cost per 1M tokens" calculation and show how concurrency affects it (we expect higher variance under bursty traffic).
3) For the CloudScale runs, Acme will run their managed endpoint (we don't want to expose VPC peering for the initial bench). Tom, can you confirm CloudScale will accept the Redwood-driven load for the agreed windows?

We can share the remaining 30 prompts by EOD today. No IP constraints on these example prompts.

Schedule: the week of 21 Sep is perfect. Would prefer the final readout on Sep 24 if possible.

  * Test IDs (A1 baseline CloudScale, B1 Redwood default FP32, B2 Redwood quantized FP16, B3 Redwood cached-prefix enabled)
  * Sequence lengths: 64 / 256 / 1024
  * Concurrency profiles: steady 50 RPS, burst pattern (peaks to 300 RPS for 30s every 5 min), and ramp test to bandwidth limits
  * Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, 95th and 99th percentile tokens/sec per GPU, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens (estimate for both managed and reserved pricing)
  * Data collection: ensure aligned timestamping, same seeding, and deterministic prompt ordering where relevant

- Identify infra needs (any reserved nodes, model variants to pin, quantization flags) and call out anything that might delay the start date of Sep 21

Keep the test matrix conservative for the first run so we can get a clean baseline; we can expand after the first readout. I put the draft plan and metrics spec in the shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-bench

Adding our proposed test matrix and a couple practical notes. I kept IDs concise so we can reference them in the readout.

Proposed tests (first sprint):
- A1 (CloudScale baseline): managed endpoint, gen-large, run across seq=[64,256,1024], steady=50 RPS, burst windows as described.
- B1 (Redwood baseline FP32): hosted, same concurrency and prompts.
- B2 (Redwood quantized FP16): same as B1 but quantized model profile.
- B3 (Redwood cached-prefix): enable prefix KV cache for repeated context in the prompt set to measure effective tokens/sec improvement.

Measurement windows: 10m steady runs per seq length + 15m burst window sequence tests; capture warmup and steady-state separately.

Primary reporting fields (results-template.csv): test_id, seq_len, run_type, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_gpu_sec_95, tokens_per_gpu_sec_99, gpu_util_pct, est_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, notes

Infrastructure notes / blockers:
- We should request one r5-reserved pool for Redwood runs to ensure steady GPU allocation (reduces p99 variance). Grace, can you check capacity for Sep 21?
- For CloudScale, since Acme will run their managed endpoint, we need clear time windows to avoid noisy neighbors; Tom, please confirm available windows and any rate-limiting thresholds.
- I’ll push the run scripts and results-template.csv to the drive folder by EOD today.

Attachments (stubs): runbook.sh (bash run driver, 6KB), results-template.csv (1KB).

If that looks right I’ll provision the reserved pool and start the smoke runs on Sep 21 morning.
